intro: We hold a recorded main-programme fee of up to ₹{{budget}} lakh for {{count}} published Mass-Communication colleges in India. This list of the best Mass-Communication colleges under ₹{{budget}} lakh is made up entirely of private colleges in our records.

Dr Zakir Husain Institute, Patna, is listed first with a Bachelor of Journalism and Mass Communication at ₹15,000. Amity University, Patna, follows with B.A. Journalism and Mass Communication at ₹32,000.
Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh have the most listings. SET and GGSIPU CET are the only recorded entrance tests, and most colleges are untagged.
listLead: These are the top Mass-Communication colleges in India 2026 with a recorded main-programme fee of up to ₹1 lakh. Titles vary between BJMC and B.A. Journalism, so compare the official award, not only the fee.
snapshot: Across {{feeN}} published colleges with a recorded fee, the median total is {{feeMedian}}, and the middle half sits between {{feeP25}} and {{feeP75}}.
All {{published}} colleges are private. Two records have a fee band that can exceed ₹1 lakh even though the minimum is under the cap.
Patna, Indore, Delhi, Gwalior and Noida appear more than once. A city count is not a measure of newsroom training quality.
firstCollegesLead: Rayat Bahra Institute of Management, Hoshiarpur, and CT Group of Institutions, Jalandhar, have recorded BJMC fees of ₹35,000 and ₹38,850. Confirm whether those official fees are annual.
Amity University, Patna, has a 2023 average package of ₹5 lakh in our records. That figure is historical and may not be published for every journalism batch.

sections.heading: What a journalism fee under ₹1 lakh may miss
paragraphs: Studio, lab and fieldwork charges are often billed separately. A low tuition can still leave a larger official bill.
If you need a university degree title, check whether the official award is BJMC, B.A. Journalism, or another variant before you apply.

compare.heading: How to compare the best Mass-Communication colleges under ₹1 lakh
paragraphs: Private journalism colleges at this budget differ widely in studios, internships and university affiliation. The recorded fee is only the first filter.
bullets: The official award and duration, and whether the fee is annual or for the full course.
Affiliation and approval, plus any studio or workshop charges.
The admission test, including SET or a university CET where it applies.
The official campus city, because Patna, Indore, Meerut and Delhi living costs differ.

faqs.question: How many mass-communication colleges have fees under ₹1 lakh here?
faqs.answer: We list {{published}} published Mass-Communication colleges with a recorded main-programme fee up to ₹{{budget}} lakh. All of them are private in our records.

faqs.question: What is a typical fee on this list?
faqs.answer: The median recorded total is {{feeMedian}}, and the middle half falls between {{feeP25}} and {{feeP75}}. Confirm the official full-course fee and any studio charges.

faqs.question: Are there public mass-communication colleges on this list?
faqs.answer: Not in our current published set. All {{published}} colleges here are recorded as private, so a public-university journalism department would appear only if we hold a qualifying fee for it.

faqs.question: What programme does the first college offer?
faqs.answer: Dr Zakir Husain Institute, Patna, is listed with a Bachelor of Journalism and Mass Communication at ₹15,000. Confirm the official duration and fee notice before you treat that as a three-year total.

faqs.question: Is this a ranking of the best Mass-Communication colleges under ₹1 lakh?
faqs.answer: No. It is a fee filter. Internships, studios and affiliation should guide the shortlist along with the official fee.
